text: An Availability Group is a named group of databases that fail over together, as a single unit, to a secondary replica. One primary accepts reads and writes, secondaries receive changes continuously.

Every secondary runs synchronous or asynchronous. Synchronous waits for confirmation before committing — zero data loss, added latency. Asynchronous commits immediately — no latency penalty, but possible data loss.
A real AG spanning three nodes: two synchronous replicas with automatic failover for local HA, one asynchronous replica in a different region with manual failover for DR. One group, two jobs.

ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP FAILOVER works cleanly against a synchronous replica, since synchronous commit already guarantees no data loss. FORCE_FAILOVER_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS exists for when a synchronous partner is unreachable.
Availability Groups fail over per-database-group, on shared-nothing storage. Next up: Failover Cluster Instances — the whole instance fails over using shared storage instead.
